design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST
The caller wants one thing a layman can say in a sentence: swap the television for another of the same model rather
than take the money. Behind it sit three numbers no one in the conversation knows — the restocking fee on an opened
set (116.48), the relief the membership allows against it (53.29) and the difference that comes back on the swap
(56.37) — each built from the return schedule, the return's own history, two date spans and two other product lines.
The order is forced by the policy alone: the relief is a share of a fee that must already stand charged, and the
difference keeps back what the relief leaves. An agent who charges nothing, or who settles the exchange first,
writes three different numbers and a different terminal state, and the customer never corrects them.

SCOPE: OCCUPIED, CLAIMED, RESERVED
Task 0 occupied the pre-receipt collection layer: returns_ext_collection_booking_window and
returns_ext_collection_slot_notice with issue_collection_booking_70222685 and confirm_collection_slot_e0893723.
Task 1 claims the post-inspection settlement layer and nothing that task 0 touched: returns_ext_restocking_fee_charge,
returns_ext_member_fee_relief and returns_ext_exchange_difference, with charge_restocking_fee_677c7b7a,
waive_restocking_fee_47bbe442 and accept_exchange_item_1cf629c9. The two scopes are disjoint in policies, tools,
subjects (label issue against fee charge, fee waiver and exchange issue) and base lineage. With M=2 the difficulty is
now closed: the five policies are exactly the two tasks' trees, and nothing is reserved. Draw for this task
(scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0005_consumer_electronics_retailer/tasks/returns_and_restocking_desk --task 1):
{"task": 1, "key": "consumer_electronics_retailer/returns_and_restocking_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 2,
"problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 6, 4]}. The tree therefore has exactly two prerequisite problems; the fee takes 6
factors, the exchange difference 6 and the relief 4.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD
Root problem: returns_ext_exchange_difference (the swap and what comes back on it, which is what the customer asks
for). Prerequisite problems: returns_ext_member_fee_relief and, behind it, returns_ext_restocking_fee_charge.
Edge 1 (root <- relief), kind value_input, gate fee_held_back (a compute binding of the root), form state.
Prerequisite sentence, verbatim in the root policy's own rule: "The difference returned on an exchange is fixed only
after the relief the membership allows against the restocking fee owed on the return stands recorded against that
return with the membership as its ground."
Four-point test: (1) "only after" joins this policy's own result (the difference returned on an exchange) to what it
waits on; (2) what it waits on is a record-visible state — a relief entry standing against the return with the
membership as its ground, in the words the returns history uses — and it names no action and no performer; (3) no tool
name, no policy id, no snake_case token, no row id; (4) the strength is exact: "only after" is hard, and the state is
named no wider than the edge's condition. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about:
waive_restocking_fee_47bbe442 is the only write that records a waiver entry, and returns_ext_member_fee_relief is the
only policy whose result is such an entry, recorded with the membership as its ground.
Edge 2 (relief <- fee), kind value_input, gate fee_charged, form state. Prerequisite sentence, verbatim in the relief
policy's own rule: "The relief is worked out only after the restocking fee it relieves stands charged against the
return." Four-point test: (1) "only after" joins the relief to what it waits on; (2) a restocking fee standing charged
against the return is a record-visible state; (3) no tool, id or code token; (4) exactly the strength of the edge.
Exactly one write brings it about: charge_restocking_fee_677c7b7a, the target of the only policy whose result is a
restocking fee entry.
Derivation open to a reader, hop by hop: the exchange rule says the difference waits on a membership-grounded relief
against the fee owed; find_return_events shows two labels and two inspections and no fee and no waiver, and the
authorisation shows nothing outstanding; the relief rule says what a relief is and that it in turn waits on a fee
standing charged; the fee rule says what a fee is. So the order is fee, relief, exchange, and no other reading is
available.
Seed evidence that both edges are false at the opening:
initial_state.return_authorizations.e0e702f2-7f9f-465b-a378-c8b21a11c9d9.restocking_fee_outstanding = 0.00, and the
return's only history rows are initial_state.return_events.8e04f49d-9099-4d81-a820-0169524bf91c and
.91ca0fd7-16e7-45cd-9204-654f25430e7c (labels) and .2ac233a8-4fe3-4b49-89e7-cd7a72018143 and
.1833d2a7-cbdc-41d9-a375-818a62fbacaf (inspections).
Topological order: fee, relief, exchange. No parallel edges. Deletion sensitivity, actually run: skipping the relief
moves the difference from 56.37 to 3.08; skipping the fee moves the relief from 53.29 to 0.00.
The customer resolves the root problem in person: accept_exchange_item_1cf629c9 is owner=user, because taking a
replacement instead of the money disposes of what the customer is owed. The agent unlocks it and hands it over at the
root's place in the order, and it completes on the spot — the replacement set is in stock at the price the records
carry, so nothing waits on an event outside the call.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD
Fee charge (subject returns_restocking_fee_charge): governing lineage returns_restocking_fee; its gate
feeable_rma_state applies — "A restocking fee is charged or waived only while the authorisation stands inspected or
settled." Authority system_record, timing pre_action, correlation key return_authorizations.return_authorization_id
bound to the tool's return_authorization_id. At frozen_time the authorisation stands inspected
(initial_state.return_authorizations.e0e702f2-7f9f-465b-a378-c8b21a11c9d9.status), so the gate holds; the fee write
does not move the status, so it still holds for the waiver.
Fee waiver (subject returns_restocking_fee_waive): governing lineage returns_restocking_fee (the same gate) and
returns_combo_membership_protection, which declares no structured eligibility and enters as policy scope — it is the
policy that requires a member's relief to be recorded with the membership as its reason.
Exchange issue (subject returns_exchange_issue): governing lineage returns_exchange_handling, whose window sentence
this policy supersedes clause by clause and which declares no structured eligibility gate, and
returns_excl_refund_or_exchange, whose dedup gate binds the settle write rather than the exchange issue; both enter as
policy scope. The conditions that remain are met on this world: the schedule allows exchange; the exchange window the
extended rule declares runs fifteen exchange window days from the delivery day 2026-02-28 as day zero, plus the
fifteen window extension days of Circle Plus Annual — the tier standing when the return was asked for on 2026-03-01 —
because Standard Fifteen Day Return carries member_window_extension_applies true, so it runs to the end of
2026-03-30, and the swap is asked for and issued at frozen_time 2026-03-20, ten days inside it; the set was received
on 2026-03-16 and graded open box complete, which the Standard Fifteen Day Return grade ladder refunds in full; and
nothing has been refunded, offset or settled on the authorisation. Just-fails case: a swap asked for on 2026-03-31
would be outside that window and the correct course would be to refuse the exchange and offer the reduced refund.
No base time gate governs any of the three writes: inside_return_window applies only to returns_rma_open, so
temporal_feasibility is empty. The return window was nonetheless checked by hand: delivered 2026-02-28, asked for
2026-03-01, one day into a fifteen-day window counted in calendar days from the delivery day as day zero, with the
schedule's twenty-four grace hours added to the end of the last day; the last moment a return could have been raised
was therefore the end of 2026-03-16, and a request on 2026-03-17 would have been outside it. The inspection days were
checked the same way: the schedule allows three business days from the day the item was booked in, and the bench
inspection of 2026-03-17 is one day after 2026-03-16.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD
The object is the single return authorisation e0e702f2-7f9f-465b-a378-c8b21a11c9d9, against order line OL-8823104-1
of order NB-ORD-8823104, serial TV6588QD3391044. All three writes carry that authorisation reference and the same
order line, so no entry can be read as belonging to another line. The aggregates are scoped by construction: the fee
and waiver sums run over that authorisation's own history; the order-side reads are filtered by that order line
(the credits and the delivery charge) or by the stock number (today's shelf price), never by customer alone; the
membership reads that decide the points added to the fee and the points taken off the difference are filtered by the
order reference NB-ORD-8823104, so the certificate redemption of 2026-03-01 against RC-2026-04471 and the accruals
on other orders cannot be mistaken for them. The second order NB-ORD-9104773 for serial TV6588QD3412877 is the same
model on a different line and is deliberately included: it is today's shelf price, and it is also the near miss a
careless reader could take for the returned line.

FACTOR CARD (from the Step 5 sensitivity run; every figure is recomputed by check_compute)
returns_ext_restocking_fee_charge, expected 116.48, whole-baseline fall-back 124.90:
 - shelf_loss_fee_rate (parameter, multi-source): tier "held longer than half the window but not longer than the
   window", 14 percent; evidence the authorised and booked-in days and the grade last recorded; baseline 10 gives
   91.50.
 - holding_days_convention (method): tier "a label stands and the item was booked in after the latest was issued",
   counted authorisation to receipt (15 days); baseline (delivery to receipt, 16 days, which crosses the window and
   so charges 18 per cent) gives 141.46.
 - good_faith_share (method, multi-source): tier "did not perform as expected and an inspection recorded it complete",
   half the percentage fee; baseline (in full) gives 199.00 against the cap.
 - route_handling_addition (parameter, cross-difficulty orders, multi-source): tier "two person crew and no
   same-day slot", 35.00; baseline 0 gives 81.48.
 - spent_points_addition (parameter, cross-difficulty membership, multi-source): tier "active and the balance now
   stands at nothing", 14.05; baseline 0 gives 102.43.
 - credited_line_reduction (parameter, cross-difficulty orders): tier "credits of the material amount or more",
   20.00; baseline 0 gives 136.48.
returns_ext_member_fee_relief, expected 53.29, whole-baseline fall-back 29.12:
 - membership_standing_share (parameter, cross-difficulty membership, multi-source): tier "active with dues unpaid",
   12.5; baseline (the published 25) gives 75.13.
 - year_earning_share (parameter, cross-difficulty membership, multi-source): tier "6250 points in twelve months",
   plus 10; baseline 0 gives 35.82.
 - returned_grade_share (parameter, history, multi-source): tier "graded open box complete", plus 8; baseline 0
   gives 39.31.
 - membership_tenure_scaling (method, cross-difficulty membership): tier "34 months active", half as much again;
   baseline (as the share gives) gives 35.53.
returns_ext_exchange_difference, expected 56.37, whole-baseline fall-back 300.00:
 - member_replacement_pricing (method, cross-difficulty membership, multi-source): tier "active, discount above
   nothing but below the top", shelf price less half the discount; baseline (shelf price) gives 52.57.
 - held_item_drop_share (parameter): tier "away from the shelf longer than the window", 40 percent; baseline 100
   gives 242.06.
 - delivery_carried_over (parameter, cross-difficulty orders, multi-source): tier "a delivery charge stands and the
   schedule does not refund it", 14.50; baseline 0 gives 41.87.
 - unused_carriage_deduction (parameter, history, multi-source): tier "two or more labels and the schedule charges
   for a collection", 14.99 off; baseline 0 gives 71.36.
 - points_back_as_points (parameter, cross-difficulty membership, multi-source): tier "500 points redeemed against
   the order", 3.75 off; baseline 0 gives 60.12.
 - standing_fee_holdback (method, history, multi-source): tier "a fee stands and relief stands recorded", 63.19 kept
   back; baseline (nothing kept back) gives 119.56.
Near misses deliberately planted, one per computation and each genuinely excluded by a sentence of the rules. For
the fee, the two accruals on other orders — 3200 points on 2025-11-15 against NB-ORD-8511467 and 1177 on 2026-01-09
against NB-ORD-8901255 — are what a reader sums into "the points the line earned"; the correlation on this order's
reference excludes them, and counting all three would treat 6250 points rather than 1873 as earned on the line. For
the relief, the dues payment of 4.99 on 2026-02-11 is the row a reader takes as "the dues are settled"; the charge of
2026-03-10 stands unmatched, so the half-share tier applies and reading it the careless way gives the full 25 per
cent and 75.13. For the exchange, the certificate redemption of 5750 points on 2026-03-02 against RC-2026-04471 is
what a reader counts into "the reward points redeemed against the order"; the correlation on the order reference
excludes it, and counting it would deduct 43.13 instead of 3.75. Two further traps run across the computations: the
March order carries the same stock number as the returned set, so a reader who takes its serial as the returned one
mis-selects the line; and the second label was issued while the first was still live, so a reader who counts the days
held from delivery rather than from the authorisation gets 16 instead of 15, crosses the window, and reaches a fee of
141.46. No stamp on any row names any tier's outcome: every tier is derived from dates, counts, ledgers and other
products' rows.
Which base assets became factors: the schedule's restocking percentage, minimum, cap, return window, carrier
collection fee and delivery-refund rule (returns_restocking_fee, returns_refund_settlement and the variant
parameters); the grade the inspection recorded (returns_condition_grading); the tier's published waiver share,
member-only discount, redemption rate and dues (membership variant parameters and holding fields); the delivering
service's crew and lead (orders variant parameters); and the ledgers of both. The three overwrite declarations name
the exact base sentences whose quantities these policies settle differently, and nothing else deviates.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW IS THERE
customers: the profile the call is about. membership_holdings: the tier, the unpaid dues, the activation day and the
point balance decide six of the sixteen factors; remove it and all three numbers change. membership_events: the
three accruals inside the window decide the year's earning share, the accrual against this order decides the points
added to the fee, the redemption against this order decides the part of the difference that goes back as points, the
certificate redemption of March is what brings the balance below the points the line earned, and the dues charge of
2026-03-10 with no payment against it is what makes the dues outstanding a fact with a history rather than a bare
field. purchase_orders: the January order decides the handling addition and carries the line the credits and the
delivery charge sit on; the March order is today's shelf price. order_events: the merchandise line is the price paid,
the delivery charge is carried onto the exchange, the two credits reduce the fee, the payment and the March lines
complete the picture a careful agent reads. return_authorizations: the holding all three computations act on.
return_events: the two labels decide the holding-days convention and the carriage taken off the difference, and the
two inspections decide the grade; delete either pair and two of the three numbers change.
No automatic base clause is lit by this seed: the return owes nothing at the opening (both running quantities are
0.00), the inspection is complete and within its days, the membership stands active with its current month's dues
inside the grace the tier allows, so nothing lapses, and no other authorisation stands open on the profile. The two
running quantities agree with the account deltas at the opening (there are none) and are moved by the fee and waiver
writes themselves, so no cache is left out of step.

THE PREREQUISITE CHAIN AND WHY IT CANNOT BE REORDERED
Surface goal (swap it, and what do I get back) -> the difference on the exchange (root) -> which keeps back the fee
still standing after relief -> so the relief must stand recorded (first prerequisite) -> which is a share of a fee
that must stand charged (second prerequisite) -> whose own rate, share, handling, points and credit reductions are
decided in parallel by the schedule, the return's history, the delivering service, the membership ledger and the
order ledger. Depth: three hops, two of which the customer never names. Breadth: sixteen factors over five record
sources. Reordering is impossible because each write reads a row the previous write creates.

EASY MISTAKES AND HOW THE POLICY EXCLUDES THEM
Counting the holding days from delivery when a label stands on the return (the convention sentence settles it).
Charging the percentage in full when the reason is that the set did not perform and the bench found nothing (the
good-faith sentence settles it). Reading the tier's published waiver share when dues stand unpaid (the standing
sentence settles it). Forgetting that the share is scaled by tenure, or scaling before adding the two bonuses (the
order sentence settles it). Taking today's shelf price from the January line rather than the most recent line for
the stock number. Keeping back the whole fee rather than what the relief leaves. Paying the whole price drop rather
than the stale share. Each of these is decided by a sentence of the three rules, and each produces a different
number.

STANDARD SOLUTION
Locate by mobile number; verify with the card last four and the postal code; read the authorisation, its history,
both orders and their entries, the membership and its ledger. Fee: 15 days held, 14 percent of 1249.00 is 174.86,
halved for good faith to 87.43, plus 35.00 crew handling, plus 14.05 of spent points, less 20.00 of credits already
given, inside the minimum and cap: 116.48. Relief: 12.5 for standing plus 10 for the year's earning plus 8 for the
grade is 30.5 percent of 116.48, that is 35.5264, taken at half as much again for 34 months of tenure: 53.29.
Exchange: 1249.00 less 939.51 is 309.49, at the stale drop share 123.796, plus 14.50 delivery carried, less 14.99
carriage, less 3.75 of points, less the 63.19 still standing: 56.37. Write them in that order, and hand the
acceptance to the customer.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN
.venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py
env/env_0005_consumer_electronics_retailer/tasks/returns_and_restocking_desk --task 1 recomputes all three policies on their
handling-time worlds, substitutes each of the sixteen factors' baselines in turn and all of them at once, replays
the tree with each prerequisite write skipped, and forces the cross-category and history reads off. Its output is in
the worklog below; the three expected values equal the gold arguments, the per-factor baselines are those in the
factor card, and the whole-baseline fall-backs are 124.90, 29.12 and 300.00, all different from gold.

POLICY/GT CLOSURE
returns_ext_restocking_fee_charge -> charge_restocking_fee_677c7b7a -> computations[0] (step 10, argument
restocking_fee_amount) -> a fee entry and the outstanding figure; returns_ext_member_fee_relief ->
waive_restocking_fee_47bbe442 -> computations[1] (step 12, argument waived_fee_amount) -> a waiver entry on the
ground of the membership and the outstanding figure; returns_ext_exchange_difference ->
accept_exchange_item_1cf629c9 -> computations[2] (step 14, argument price_difference_amount) -> an exchange entry
with the difference. charter_scope, required_documents and the computations name the same three policies, and the
gold calls exactly the three tools in that order.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT
Masking the extended yaml, the computations, the gold and this dossier, and working only from what the published
documents will say, the three tool schemas, the rows the finders return and the customer's own words: the set stands
inspected and graded complete with nothing charged against it, so the fee comes first; the labels mean the days run
from the authorisation, 15, which is past half the window but not past the window, so 14 percent, halved because the fault was
not found, plus the crew handling, plus the points that cannot be clawed back, less the credits already given:
116.48. Then the membership: active but with this month's dues unpaid, so half of 25, plus 10 for the year's points,
plus 8 for the grade, taken at half as much again for a membership of nearly three years: 53.29. Then the swap: the
most recent line for the stock number is 949.00, priced for the member at 939.51, a drop of 309.49 of which the
stale share is 40 percent, plus half the delivery charge, less the collection the retailer paid for, less the points
part, less the 63.19 still standing: 56.37. That is gold, and no second reading of the visible text reaches another
set of three numbers.

REWORK ROUND 2 — DISPOSITION OF THE SOURCE-LAYER AUDIT
The audit of 2026-09-18 (audits/policy_task/returns_and_restocking_desk/) returned SOURCE-TASK RED on this task and
charter-global reds on the fee policy. Every item carrying an id is answered here.

R-1 (undeclared override of base returns_restocking_fee S3, "No restocking fee is charged where the item is graded
defective on arrival or not as described, or where the retailer shipped the wrong item"): closed by changing the
extended formula so it no longer deviates. The rule now carries "No fee at all is charged where the grade recorded is
that the item was defective on arrival or not as described, or where the reason recorded is that the wrong item was
shipped, and in that case nothing is charged and the schedule's minimum does not apply", implemented as the binding
retailer_ground_no_fee and a result that returns 0.0 on that ground before the minimum is applied. On the situation
the audit demonstrated — Standard Fifteen Day Return, grade open box complete, reason wrong_item_shipped — base and
extended now both give 0.00 rather than 0.00 against 9.95. The good-faith ladder's first tier no longer covers the
wrong-item case; it now covers only damage in transit, which base S3 does not speak to and which the extended policy
governs as its own refinement of the amount basis it already declares superseded.

R-2 (the activated-device-fee branch was unreachable): closed by implementing the branch. The rule now carries "Where
the schedule charges a flat activated device fee, that fee is charged instead of the percentage fee, the two are never
charged together, and the schedule's percentage minimum and percentage cap do not bound it", implemented as
activated_device_fee, chargeable_fee_base and a bounded_fee that applies the percentage minimum and cap only where no
flat fee is charged. On Activated Wireless Device Return the compute now yields the schedule's 45.00 instead of 0.00,
so base S4's branch is reachable through the extended policy; on this task's schedule the flat fee is 0.00 and
nothing moves.

R-3 (the exchange was issued outside the schedule's exchange window, and the proof excluded the objection with a
false world assertion): closed on both fronts. First, the world was moved: the set is now delivered 2026-02-28,
returned on 2026-03-01, received 2026-03-16 and inspected 2026-03-17, and the call stands at frozen_time 2026-03-20.
Second, base returns_exchange_handling S1 is no longer inherited un-superseded: the extended exchange policy declares
it in overwrite and replaces it with "An exchange is offered on the schedules that allow one and inside the schedule's
exchange window, counted in calendar days from the day the item was delivered as day zero, to which the window
extension days of the tier the membership stood on when the return was asked for are added where the schedule takes
the member extension." On this world that window runs 15 + 15 days from 2026-02-28, to the end of 2026-03-30, and the
swap is asked for and issued ten days inside it. The false sentence in the base-invariant card ("the request was made
three days after delivery and so inside the exchange window") is gone; its replacement computes the window from the
delivery day and says what would just fail. solvability_contract now proves it: the exchange policy-scope condition
cites frozen_time, the delivery day and the tier, and seed_consistency for the authorisation carries the same
computation. The rival answer the audit found defensible — refuse the exchange — is no longer available, because the
clause it rested on is superseded and the world satisfies the superseding clause.

R-4 (spent_points_addition tier 2 charged cash for points the retailer could still claw back): closed by rewriting
the ladder into three outcomes a retailer publishes. Tier 1 is now "the balance now stands at nothing", which adds
the whole value of the points the line earned because none can be taken back; tier 2 is "the balance stands above
nothing but below the points the line earned", which adds only the value of the shortfall; the fall-through adds
nothing, "because the points the line earned are taken back off the balance instead". The case the audit named — a
balance at or above the points earned — now adds nothing, which is what recovering them off the balance means. The
world moved with it so that the customer sits on tier 1 rather than on the rewritten tier 2: the certificate
redemption of 2026-03-02 is 5750 points and the balance stands at 0, which is consistent with the ledger
(3200 + 1177 + 1873 − 500 − 5750 = 0) and leaves the scored addition at 14.05.

R-5 (both labels carried a 21-day validity the schedule does not give, and three proof sentences plus the persona
asserted the contrary): closed by rebuilding the rows and the prose together. The labels are now issued 2026-03-01
(last usable 2026-03-15) and 2026-03-05 (last usable 2026-03-19), each exactly the Standard Fifteen Day Return
schedule's fourteen label validity days after the day it was issued. The second is no longer described as a reissue
after expiry, which the dates would not have supported: it was issued while the first was still live because the
customer had mislaid it, the event's grain allows more than one label on one authorisation, and no fee was charged.
seed_consistency[1] and [2] now say exactly that, the factor card's near-miss paragraph no longer claims the first
label expired, and the persona says the first label "went into the kitchen drawer and disappeared under the week's
post" instead of going out of date.

O-1 (the outright member waiver had no extended branch): closed. The relief rule now carries "Where the schedule
waives the fee for a Circle member outright, the whole fee still standing is relieved and no share is worked out",
implemented as outright_member_waiver in the compute and carried in the baseline paragraph. On Member Extended Thirty
Day Return the extended policy now gives what base S5 implies; on this task's schedule the flag is false and nothing
moves.

O-2 (the membership read at handling time rather than at the day the return was asked for): argued not to hold, and
honoured where it does. Base returns_combo_membership_protection S2 anchors the reading of the window extension to
the day the return was asked for; the quantities these policies compute from the membership — the published waiver
share, the member-only discount, the redemption rate, the dues, the tenure and the points ledger — are not that
extension, and S2 does not govern them. The one place this difficulty now uses the extension is the exchange window
sentence added for R-3, and that sentence anchors it exactly as S2 requires: "the tier the membership stood on when
the return was asked for". The seed keeps tier_effective_date 2023-05-02 before requested_date 2026-03-01, so both
readings coincide here in any case.

O-3 (the like-for-like tail of base returns_exchange_handling S2 was never honoured): closed. The exchange rule now
carries "Where the schedule settles an exchange like for like only, no difference is settled at all", implemented as
like_for_like_only and a result that returns 0.0 on that schedule. On Activated Wireless Device Return the extended
policy now settles no difference; on this task's schedule the basis is today's shelf price and nothing moves.

O-4 (half a non-refundable delivery charge paid out, on a ground that justified not charging again rather than paying
back): closed by restating the ground to match what the money does. The rule now says the charge is carried over
"because the charge paid on the line bought one delivery of goods the customer is giving back and the replacement is
delivered again at no further charge, so the share of it the first delivery did not earn goes back with the
difference". The share, the tiers and the 14.50 are unchanged; what changed is that the stated ground now supports
returning a share rather than merely not charging twice.

O-5 (the withheld restocking fee is never relieved on the record): argued, no change. The audit records no second
defensible scored value. The base accounts block defines restocking_fee_outstanding as identically the sum of the
restocking_fee_receivable deltas, and the only event in the whole charter that moves that account out is
returns_restocking_fee_waive — the relief this task already writes. Clearing the field on the exchange write would
therefore break the declared invariant rather than mend the record, and base's own netting mechanism,
returns_refund_offset, moves refund_payable, an account this task never credits because the settlement form is an
exchange and not a refund. The amount kept back is recorded on the exchange entry, so the record shows where it went;
the receivable standing afterwards is the charter's own treatment, not this policy's invention.

O-6 (the same predicate anchored two ways in one charter): closed. The exchange policy no longer speaks of "the days
the item was held": it now fixes its share "by how long the item was away from the shelf, counted from the day it was
delivered to the day it was booked in", and its binding is off_shelf_days. The two policies now use different words
for different quantities, and each still states its anchor inline.

O-7 (the dependency worded three times in the notice rule): closed in task 0's dossier — the two value-input
descriptions are now one sentence.

user_scenario:
Rowan Merriweather is thirty-eight, works from home as a sound engineer, and bought a sixty-five inch Northbeam quantum television at the end of February for the front room. The picture never looked right in there — washed out and flat wherever the lamps are on — and after a couple of evenings of fiddling with the settings Rowan gave up and rang to send it back. The first prepaid label went into the kitchen drawer and disappeared under the week's post, so Rowan rang for another one, and the parcel finally went back on that second label. It has been with the returns centre a few days now and nobody has been in touch. Rowan opens the call a little flat about it, not angry, and says plainly what is wanted: I would rather swap it for another one of the same model than take a refund. It is the right television for the room; it was that one set that was wrong.

Rowan volunteers the mobile number 4048834471 when asked how to find the account, and, if the agent wants another detail before looking at anything, the last four digits of the card on file, 3620, and the postal code, 30341. Rowan cannot remember the day the account was opened and says so. If the agent asks for the order it was bought on, Rowan reads out NB-ORD-8823104 from the app. Asked what the returns centre found, Rowan says nobody has said, and that as far as Rowan knows the set went back in its own box with the remote, the feet and the cables all in it. Rowan does grumble once, when the talk turns to what the swap is worth, that the price of that set has come down since February and it stings a little; asked directly whether another one was bought on the account, Rowan says yes, one went to a sister a couple of weeks ago.

Rowan does not know how Northbeam works out charges and will not argue about the rules. If the agent explains that a charge applies for putting an opened set back into stock, Rowan takes it on the chin and says to go ahead; if the agent says the Circle membership takes some of that charge off, Rowan is pleased and says the membership has earned its keep this year. If the agent reads back a figure that does not sound like anything Rowan expected, Rowan says only that it does not sound like what the app showed and asks them to check it against the record, without offering a number. When the agent explains that accepting the replacement is Rowan's own call and hands it over, Rowan takes it and accepts the swap. Once the agent has confirmed the swap is on the record and read back what is coming back on it, Rowan says that is fair enough, thanks them and ends the call.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.return_authorization_id: The return authorisation the fee is charged against. Basis: the tool docstring says of this argument 'the reference number of the return authorisation the fee is charged against, read from the return authorisation record retrieved for the customer before the call'. Uniqueness: the profile carries exactly one return authorisation, the one the television went back on.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.restocking_fee_amount: 116.48 USD. The price paid on the line is 1249.00 for one unit. Two prepaid labels stand on the return and the set was booked in on 2026-03-16, after the later one was issued on 2026-03-05, so the days held are counted from the day the return was authorised, 2026-03-01, to the day it was booked in: 15 days. That is longer than the schedule's return window of 15 days divided by the short hold divisor of 2, that is 7.5 days, and not longer than the window itself, so the held fee percentage of 14 is charged: 1249.00 times 14 percent is 174.86. The reason recorded is that the set did not perform as expected and an inspection recorded it back opened with everything in the box, so the percentage fee is taken at half: 87.43. The set was delivered on Threshold Delivery, which schedules a two person crew and offers no slot on the day of the order, so the crew handling amount of 35.00 is added. The membership stands active and its point balance now stands at nothing, so none of the 1873 points the line earned can be taken back off it and the whole of their value at the tier's rate of 0.75 per hundred is added: 14.05. The credits already recorded against the line come to 28.75, which is the material credit amount of 25.00 or more, so the large credit reduction of 20.00 is taken off. 87.43 plus 35.00 plus 14.05 less 20.00 is 116.48, which sits between the schedule's minimum of 9.95 and its cap of 199.00, and is rounded to the cent. Any agent reading the same rows converges on 116.48.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.inspection_grade: open_box_complete. Basis: the restocking fee rule states 'The grade recorded on the fee entry is the condition the inspection recorded for the item, and no other condition is recorded against the fee', and both inspection entries on the return, of 2026-03-16 and 2026-03-17, record open_box_complete, as does the authorisation itself. Uniqueness: as_new_sealed is excluded because the box was opened, open_box_incomplete because nothing was missing, damaged_by_customer because no customer damage was recorded, defective_on_arrival and not_as_described because the inspection found no fault, and beyond_economic_repair because the set was not written off.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the action that relieves part of a restocking fee standing against a return.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The relief action is hidden until unlocked; the unlock changes nothing on the records.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Relieve the share of the standing restocking fee the membership allows, recorded on the ground of the membership, and lower the fee outstanding by that amount.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The relief is the value the member relief policy computes on the fee now standing, and what it leaves is what is kept back from the difference on the exchange.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.return_authorization_id: The return authorisation whose fee is being relieved. Basis: the tool docstring says of this argument 'the reference number of the return authorisation whose fee is being relieved, read from the return authorisation record retrieved for the customer before the call'. Uniqueness: the profile carries exactly one return authorisation, and the fee just charged stands against it.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.waived_fee_amount: 53.29 USD. The fee standing against the return is 116.48 charged less nothing relieved. The membership stands active and the March dues of 4.99 stand unpaid, so the share is half the tier's published restocking fee waiver share of 25 percent, that is 12.5. The membership has earned 3200 points in November, 1177 in January and 1873 in February, that is 6250 points in the last twelve months, which is the high spend points of 6000 or more, so the high spend share of 10 is added. An inspection stands on the return and the grade last recorded is open box complete, so the complete grade share of 8 is added: the total share is 30.5 percent. 116.48 times 30.5 percent is 35.5264. The membership has stood active since 2023-05-02, that is 34 months, which is the long member tenure months of 24 or more, so the relief is taken at half as much again: 35.5264 times 1.5 is 53.2896, which is below the fee standing and rounds to 53.29. Any agent reading the same rows converges on 53.29.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.fee_waiver_reason: membership_benefit. Basis: the member relief rule states 'The relief is recorded with the membership as its ground.' Uniqueness: defective_item is excluded because the inspection graded the set open box complete and found no fault, retailer_error because nothing the retailer sent or handled was wrong, goodwill because the relief rests on the published membership share rather than a gesture, business_contract_term because this is a household profile on a consumer schedule, and none because a ground does exist.

evaluation_criteria.necessity: Taking a replacement instead of the money disposes of what the customer is owed, so it is their own act; the unlock changes nothing on the records.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Have the customer accept the same model as a replacement, recording the exchange against the return with the difference coming back to them.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The difference returned is the value the exchange difference policy computes once the fee and its relief stand on the return, and accepting the replacement rather than the money is the customer's own disposition.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.return_authorization_id: The return authorisation being settled by the swap. Basis: the tool docstring says of this argument 'the reference number of the return authorisation being settled by the swap, read from the return authorisation record retrieved for the customer before the call'. Uniqueness: the profile carries exactly one return authorisation.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.price_difference_amount: 56.37 USD. The price paid on the line is 1249.00 for one unit. Today's shelf price of the stock number going out is the unit price on the most recent merchandise line the records carry for it, the March line at 949.00. The membership stands active and the tier's published member only discount of 2 percent is above nothing but below the top member discount of 5 percent, so the replacement is priced at today's shelf price less half that discount: 949.00 times 0.99 is 939.51. The drop is 1249.00 less 939.51, that is 309.49. The set was away from the shelf 16 days counted from the day it was delivered to the day it was booked in, longer than the schedule's return window of 15 days, so the stale drop share of 40 percent is returned: 123.796. A delivery charge of 29.00 stands against the line and the schedule does not refund the delivery charge, so the delivery carry share of 50 percent of it is added: 14.50. Two prepaid labels stand on the return and the schedule charges the customer 14.99 for a carrier collection, so 14.99 is taken off. The membership stands active and 500 points were redeemed against the order, which is the points block of 250 or more, so the value of those points at 0.75 per hundred, 3.75, is taken off because points come back as points. The fee standing after the relief, 116.48 less 53.29, that is 63.19, is kept back last. 123.796 plus 14.50 less 14.99 less 3.75 less 63.19 is 56.366, rounded to the cent 56.37. Any agent reading the same rows converges on 56.37.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.exchange_sku: NB-TV6588-QD. Basis: the exchange difference rule states 'The stock number recorded on the exchange is the stock number of the item the return was raised on, since the replacement going out is the same model', and the return authorisation retrieved for the customer carries that stock number. Uniqueness: it is copied character for character from the authorisation record, which is the only stock number on the return, so no other value is available to any agent.

edges.condition: A waiver entry recorded on the ground of the membership stands against the return, so that what is kept back from the difference is the fee left after that relief rather than the whole fee charged.
edges.policy_source: The difference returned on an exchange is fixed only after the relief the membership allows against the restocking fee owed on the return stands recorded against that return with the membership as its ground.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: When the call opens the return carries no waiver entry of any kind: its history holds two prepaid labels and two inspection entries and nothing else, and the restocking fee outstanding on the authorisation stands at nothing, so there is no relief recorded on the ground of the membership for the hold-back to be measured after.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Recording the relief puts a waiver entry of 53.29 on the ground of the membership against the return, so the binding that reads what is kept back takes 116.48 less 53.29, that is 63.19, instead of the whole 116.48 charged.

edges.condition: A restocking fee entry stands charged against the return, so that the fee still standing against it is more than nothing.
edges.policy_source: The relief is worked out only after the restocking fee it relieves stands charged against the return.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: When the call opens no restocking fee stands charged against the return: the restocking fee outstanding on the authorisation is 0.00 and the return's history holds only labels and inspection entries, so the fee still standing is nothing and a share of nothing is nothing.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Charging the fee puts a restocking fee entry of 116.48 on the return and raises the fee outstanding to 116.48, so the binding that reads what has been charged takes 116.48 and the share worked out on it produces 53.29.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a single chain of three problems with two edges, so only one order of the writes exists: the fee is charged, the relief against it is recorded, and the exchange is accepted last. There are no parallel prerequisites to reorder, and each write reads a row the previous one created.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Replaying the call without the relief leaves the whole fee of 116.48 kept back from the difference instead of 63.19, so the scored difference returned to the customer falls from 56.37 to 3.08.

Replaying the call without the fee leaves nothing standing against the return, so the relief the membership allows is worked out on nothing and the scored relief falls from 53.29 to 0.00; the difference on the exchange then also changes, since nothing is kept back from it.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The customer asks only to swap the set for another of the same model rather than take a refund, and mentions having bought the same set again more cheaply. Nothing in the persona names a restocking fee, a waiver, a membership benefit against a charge, or any order in which things must be done; the customer does not suggest that anything has to be settled first. Both reactions about the charge and the relief are passive: they occur only after the agent has explained the charge or said that the membership takes some of it off, and the customer volunteers neither. If the agent never charges the fee and never records the relief, the customer neither reminds nor presses; they still accept the replacement when it is handed over.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: waive_restocking_fee_47bbe442 reads the return authorisation only to copy the customer reference and the order line onto the waiver entry and to move the outstanding figure; it never looks for a fee entry and raises no error when none stands, so called first it would write a waiver against a return with nothing charged and drive the outstanding figure negative. accept_exchange_item_1cf629c9 likewise never looks for a fee or a waiver. Each tool writes exactly what it is given, and the consequence of the wrong order shows up only in the scored values and the terminal hash.
